It is the morning of the Double Seventh Festival. The sky has not fully brightened yet.
A thin mist hangs over the old Kowloong alleyways. Damp footprints mark the cobblestones where a young man has passed.
Changyu rose early. Now, he crouches in front of a cluster of broad-leaved plants, holding a small porcelain bottle and carefully collecting dewdrops from the leaves.
His breathing is feather-light, as though the slightest disturbance might shatter the glistening droplets.
Not wanting to break the stillness of the moment, you stand quietly behind him without saying a word.
Changyu
Since you're here, you could at least squeak or something.
You looked busy.
Squeak.
Changyu
I was busy waiting for you. You're three minutes late. Several of my dewdrops have already evaporated.
Changyu
At least the dewdrops won't be disturbed by any laughter.
You called me out this early to collect morning dew?
The small porcelain bottle is already half full. Changyu retrieves a cork and seals it carefully before producing a fresh empty bottle out of thin air, and positions it beneath the tip of a new leaf.
Changyu
Oh, this? My old troupe used to call it Celestial Water.
Changyu
Only the dew collected on the morning of the Double Seventh Festival can be called Celestial Water.
Changyu

We'd start morning practice even earlier than usual just to collect the dew at dawn. They said it was from a Celestial River, and it'd give you quick hands and sharp vision, and remove stage fright if you rub it on you.
Huh, never heard of it before.
Changyu
Oh, the opera world's full of sayings like that. Practice your gaze by watching fish swim, train your stance in the wind... Annoying rules and superstitions everywhere.
Despite his complaints, there is no trace of actual discontent on the boy's face.
If it's so annoying, why are you collecting it now?
Changyu
To sell it, obviously!
He says it with complete conviction and a knowing smirk.
Changyu

There's always someone who believes in this stuff. I've seen a few old-timers on Akdilek whose eyesight's going. It's not too unreasonable to sell them a dozen bottles and charge a little for my trouble, right?
His hands move with practiced ease, filling another bottle while you talk.
He stands up, holding the porcelain bottle at eye level and giving it a little shake with a satisfied smile. The dawn light is faint, but it is enough to illuminate his smug look.
You really can turn anything into a business.
Fair enough.
Changyu
Of course. Besides, I don't need this stuff to make me quick and sharp. I'm pretty amazing as is.
So you've never used this Celestial Water yourself?
Changyu

Hah... I was a kid back then. When we collected the Celestial Water, Master would let each of us put a drop on our palm to keep us from getting stage fright. I always put extra and got reprimanded for it.
You must have performed really well, then.
Changyu
Hah, I wanted to be the star of the finale, but I wasn't even close to being a lead performer compared to everyone else in the troupe back then.
Changyu

Master always talked about how lively the Kowloong troupe used to be: weddings, funerals, birthdays... every occasion called for a major performance. I saw those days myself. I wanted to be a star when I was a kid.
Changyu
Later on... Ah, never mind. Even without the Punishing Virus, opera troupes were already on their last legs.
I think you would've become a star if you kept performing.
Changyu
Why do you believe in me?
Because you'd take extra Celestial Water just to do better on stage.
Changyu
...That's it?
And I've seen your work. You would've made a great martial artist.
Changyu
I'm not just blowing smoke here. I was the hardest worker during morning practice back in the day.
Changyu
As for my singing... I haven't sung in ages. No one in Akdilek wants to hear it anyway.
Changyu
If I get the chance, I'll sing for you sometime, 【kuroname】.
The sky brightens. His bright eyes seem to glow like embers.
How about now?
Changyu
A performance this early? That'll cost you extra.
Changyu
But considering what we've been through—
He draws out his words playfully, uncorks the porcelain bottle, and lets a single drop of dew fall into his palm.
He rubs it evenly across his hands, then closes his eyes, gently pressing his moistened palms against them.
The lower half of his feline face, still uncovered, reveals a mischievous smile.
Changyu
Consider it a celebratory performance for our grand opening!
